best_for: Researchers and students who write in LaTeX or Markdown and want a free reference manager that keeps everything in a plain BibTeX file they own.

points.title: Plain text, no lock-in
points.text: JabRef stores your library as BibTeX or BibLaTeX, a plain-text format any LaTeX setup reads. Moving away later means keeping the same file.

points.title: Fill entries from an ID
points.text: Paste an ISBN, DOI, PubMed ID or arXiv ID and it fetches the details. It imports more than 15 reference formats, and browser extensions for Chrome, Firefox and Edge add references in one click.

points.title: Cite where you write
points.text: It sends citations to TeXstudio, Texmaker, LyX, Kile, WinEdt, Emacs and Vim, and inserts them in Word and LibreOffice. It can also fetch PDFs and rename and file them by your rules.

points.title: Free and open source
points.text: JabRef is MIT-licensed with no paid tier and no account.

points.title: Sandboxed packages cannot reach LibreOffice
points.text: The Snap and Flatpak builds cannot talk to outside programs such as LibreOffice. Use the .deb, .rpm or archive if you cite into LibreOffice. The Flathub package itself is verified as published by JabRef.

points.title: Version 6 is still in testing
points.text: 5.15 is the current stable release. 6.0 is in beta, and its new search index cannot be read by older versions, so going back and forth may force a long rebuild on big libraries.

points.title: Installs and history
points.text: Windows gets an x64 MSI that installs for all users; a portable zip is also offered by the project. The Windows listing keeps 15 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release.
